title: Stories about people living inside strange systems.
intro: Star Splitter Visions publishes independent speculative comics and graphic stories about people facing extraordinary circumstances, from displaced Vikings in New York to desert builders challenging a water monopoly.
paragraphs: In Vikings 2026!, ninth-century newcomers must build a life inside modern New York's rules. In Backyard Rockets, three builders challenge a company's grip on water and communications. In Rex Fleet, Commodore Ella Venn must keep a rescue from becoming a conflict between rival powers.

These stories begin with strange premises, but their drama is recognizable: friends disagree, coworkers improvise, communities depend on one another, and choices made under pressure have consequences.
The future is not only a matter of technology. People live through institutions: workplaces, cities, families, governments, and the quiet negotiations required to get through a day.
Some stories are funny. Some are quiet. Some are cosmic. What connects them is an interest in the people living inside these worlds, not just the worlds themselves.
Generative AI is used in the development and artwork of these comics, alongside creative direction, editing, and production review.
centerQuote: The future is not only built by invention. It is lived through institutions.
topPullquote: Not escapism, exactly. Recognition, displaced into another world.
principles: Humor, conflict, work, and everyday life
Stories built to be read, not just looked at
bottomPullquote: The impossible is only the beginning. The story is what people do with it.
